correctness.rationale: Huang's arbitrary-initial theorem bounds the root rate by \(\max\{|1-1/c|,|1-c_0/c|\}\). A fixed-diagonal perturbation has exact scalar error multiplier \(1-c_0/c\), while a diagonal perturbation has \(p_k=p_0^{(1-1/c)^k}\) and hence root rate \(|1-1/c|\). Thus each term is attained by explicit data, including separate treatment of the zero-factor edge cases. Equioscillation of the two affine factors gives the unique minimizer \(c=(1+c_0)/2\). No finite experiment is used as an infinite proof.

value.rationale: The claim solves the natural constant-parameter tuning problem left by the source's two-mode rate estimate. It proves that neither mode can be removed from the robust analysis, identifies the exact worst-case factor, and gives a unique rate-optimal parameter \(c=(1+c_0)/2\) for every data set. This is a reusable algorithmic design rule rather than a routine numerical instance.
